He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]]. ==High school career== Wesson is the son of Keith Wesson, who played at [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] from 1983 to 1987. Kaleb attended [[Westerville South High School]] and played alongside older brother [[Andre Wesson|Andre]]. Kaleb became a starter as a sophomore on the state runner-up team. He had seven points and four rebounds as the Wildcats beat [[Lima Senior High School]] 57–55 to claim the state title. Wesson scored a school-record 49 points in a 68–67 loss to [[Upper Arlington High School]] on January 24, 2017. As a senior, Wesson averaged 22.4 points and 10.9 rebounds per game and shot 67 percent from the floor on a team that finished 19–6. He was named [[Ohio Mr. Basketball]].{{cite news |title=Westerville South's Kaleb Wesson named AP Mr. Basketball; Jackson's Kyle Young second in voting news|url=http://btn.com/2018/02/26/view-the-2017-18-all-big-ten-mens-basketball-team/|title=View the 2017-18 All-Big Ten Men's Basketball Team|work=Big Ten Network|access-date=December 2, 2019}} Wesson had a career-high 31 points in a 75–56 win against [[Youngstown State Penguins men's basketball|Youngstown State]] on December 18, 2018.{{cite news |title=No. 15 Buckeyes overcome slow start, rout Youngstown State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082555 |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 18, 2018}} On March 1, 2019, Wesson was suspended for violating athletic department policy.{{cite magazine |last1=Abdeldaiem |first1=Alaa |title=Ohio State Suspends Kaleb Wesson for Violation of Athletics Department Policy |url=https://www.si.com/college/2019/03/01/ohio-state-suspends-kaleb-wesson-violation-policy-buckeyes |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 1, 2019}} He missed three games and returned in time for a Big Ten Tournament matchup with [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], finishing with 17 points, 13 rebounds, three assists, three blocks and two steals in the 79–75 victory.{{cite news |last1=Ryan |first1=Shannon |title=Ohio State looks more like an NCAA Tournament team with Kaleb Wesson's return |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-spt-ohio-state-kaleb-wesson-20190314-story.html |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |date=March 14, 2019}} Wesson was an [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] honorable mention selection.{{Cite web |url=http://bigten.org/news/2019/3/11/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx?path=mbball |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404171441/https://bigten.org/news/2019/3/11/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx?path=mbball |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 4, 2019 |title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN |website=BigTen.org |date=March 11, 2019 |access-date=December 2, 2019 }} As a sophomore, Wesson averaged 14.6 points, 6.9 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game, shooting 50 percent from the floor and 34 percent from three-point range. After the season, he declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]] but ultimately opted to return to Ohio State.{{cite news |last1=Phillips |first1=Scott |title=Kaleb Wesson returning to Ohio State after testing NBA draft waters |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2019/05/28/kaleb-wesson-returning-to-ohio-state-after-testing-nba-draft-waters/ |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=May 28, 2018}} Wesson worked on his conditioning coming into his junior year by boxing with strength and conditioning coach Quadrian Banks. He was ranked the sixth-best player in college basketball by ESPN in October 2019.{{cite news |last1=Gasaway |first1=John |title=Top 25 players for the 2019-20 college basketball season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/insider/story/_/id/27910283/top-25-players-2019-20-college-basketball-season |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=October 29, 2019}} After scoring 10 points and grabbing 11 rebounds in a 76–51 victory over [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], Wesson was named Big Ten player of the week on November 18.{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Patrick |title=Kaleb Wesson named Big Ten Player of the Week |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Ohio-State-Buckeyes-basketball-Kaleb-Wesson-Big-Ten-Player-of-the-Week-Weeek-3-138820049/ |accessdate=December 2, 2019 |work=247 Sports |date=November 18, 2019}} He had 28 points and 10 rebounds in a 106–74 rout of [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]], helping the Buckeyes notch 100 points against a Big Ten rival for the first time since 1991.{{cite news |title=Wesson, No. 6 Ohio State unload on Penn State 106–74 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166105 |accessdate=December 8, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 7, 2019}} At the close of the regular season, Wesson was named to the Second Team All-Big Ten by the coaches and media.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200309231733/https://bigten.org/news/2020/3/9/big-ten-unveils-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-on-btn.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 9, 2020|title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 9, 2020 |accessdate=March 9, 2020}} As a junior, Wesson averaged 14.0 points (10th in the Big Ten) and 9.3 rebounds (5th) per game, shooting 42.5% from beyond the arc, and was ninth in the Big Ten in free throw percentage, at 73.1%.{{cite news |last1=Harrison |first1=Phil |title=Ohio State big man Kaleb Wesson named second team All-Big Ten by the coaches and media |url=https://buckeyeswire.usatoday.com/2020/03/09/ohio-state-kaleb-wesson-named-second-team-all-big-ten/ |accessdate=March 24, 2020 |work=Buckeyes Wire |date=March 9, 2020}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kaleb-wesson-1.html|title=Kaleb Wesson College Stats|website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Ohio State's Kaleb Wesson entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28987297/ohio-state-kaleb-wesson-entering-nba-draft |accessdate=April 4, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 2, 2020}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Wesson signed with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-training-camp-roster-20201204|title=Warriors Announce Roster for 2020-21 Training Camp, Fueled by Gatorade|work=NBA.com|date=December 3, 2020|access-date=December 6, 2020}} On December 18, 2020, the Warriors released Wesson.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-sutton-toupane-wesson-20201218|title=Warriors Waive Forwards Sutton, Toupane and Wesson|work=NBA.com|date=December 18, 2020|access-date=December 18, 2020}} ===Santa Cruz Warriors (2021)=== On January 12, 2021, Wesson was included in roster of [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] which would participate the [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2020–21 season]] in the [[ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex]] of [[Walt Disney World|Walt Disney World Resort]] located near [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]].{{cite web|url=https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2020-21-roster|title=Santa Cruz Warriors announce 2020-21 roster|date=January 12, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 12, 2021}} ===Overseas (2021–present)=== On April 1, 2021, Wesson signed with [[B.C. Oostende|Filou Oostende]] of the [[Pro Basketball League|Belgian League]].{{cite web|last1=Chokrani|first1=Yassine|title=KALEB WESSON SIGNS WITH OOSTENDE (VIDEO)|url=https://thisisbasketball.world/kaleb-wesson-signs-with-oostende/?v=0b98720dcb2c|website=ThisIsBasketball.world|accessdate=April 3, 2021|date=April 1, 2021}} On September 9, 2021, Wesson signed with [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite news |title=Hapoel Galil Gilboa sign Tom Maayan, Kaleb Wesson |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-galil-gilboa-sign-tom-maayan-kaleb-wesson/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 9, 2021 |date=September 9, 2021|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} On January 1, 2022, Wesson signed with [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{cite web |title=Kaleb Wesson signed with Maccabi Rishon Le-Zion |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Israel/news/724467/Kaleb-Wesson-signed-with-Maccabi-Rishon-Le-Zion |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 2, 2022 |date=January 1, 2022}} In August 2022, he signed with the [[Phoenix Super LPG Fuel Masters]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) as the team's import for the [[2022–23 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/first-time-import-kaleb-weeson-to-reinforce-phoenix-a793-20220817|title=Young gun Kaleb Wesson to reinforce Phoenix in Commissioner's Cup|publisher=Spin.ph|date=August 17, 2022|accessdate=August 17, 2022}} On July 29, 2024, Wesson signed with the [[Kaohsiung Aquas]] of the [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League]] (TPBL).{{cite news |title=海神挑戰金盃 208公分新洋將加盟 |url=https://udn.com/news/story/7003/8126784 |accessdate=July 29, 2024 |work=United Daily News |date=July 29, 2024 }} On July 29, 2025, [[Kaohsiung Aquas]] announced that
